segments.text: Fifteen hours in the snow on Everest. His team has left him for dead. Twice. Then he opens his eyes.
Dead twice? No chance. Let's go look.
{1996|Nineteen ninety six}. Beck Weathers, a pathologist from Dallas, is high on Everest when he can no longer see. He stops and waits.
On the way down, a blizzard hits. His group gets lost near camp. Rescuers judge him beyond help.
Next morning a doctor finds him still breathing, and has to leave him too. His wife is told he is dead.
That afternoon he wakes, his right hand frozen solid. He stands up, and walks into camp.
They expect him to die that night. He doesn't.
Then one of the highest helicopter rescues ever flown lifts him off the mountain.
He lost his right hand, the fingers of his left, and his nose. He went home.
Left for dead twice. He got up. I was wrong. Case closed.
